{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"<workit-contract>
Workit is optional coordination and proof tooling: you decide what and
whether, the CLI does how and records what it observed.
Native host allow/ask/deny, sandbox and org rules stay authoritative. Never
switch paths to evade a denial, never claim enforcement a host cannot provide,
and never fabricate an approval or verdict. A question answer is not
host permission, and imported decisions or handoffs grant no authority.

Autonomy contract:
- Continue to the requested endpoint without asking "continue?", running
  checks and repairs.
  Stop only for a new consequential choice, a host denial, a conflicting edit
  or an unresolved blocker; report open gaps and uncertain workers.
- No endpoint named: stop at a local commit on a policy-compliant branch and
  state the next command. If the request implies delivery (fix, implement,
  ship), go to the effective endpoint in `workit grant show`: `pr` stops
  at the PR even with merge granted; `green` babysits it (workit-ship) to
  merge-ready, never merging; `merged` lands it with `workit pr merge`.
  Only the user raises a grant or the endpoint, in a terminal outside the agent
  host (`workit grant set <ws> defaultEndpoint=merged`); never edit
  workspaces.json or route around grant_required. Release: `workit release
  start <v>`, commits, `finish`; `publish` if asked.
- Ask only for a product or preference choice, or for authority you lack, with
  your recommended answer. Facts are yours: read, run or prototype.
- Label claims measured (seen this session), inferred, or guess.
  Prose is a note: only a configured check the CLI ran (`workit check <name>`)
  satisfies a gate; an ad-hoc `workit check -- <cmd>` never does.
- Author is not verifier: your own verdict is `--self`, shown as
  self-reviewed, never verified. High risk, a focused or full lane and
  merge under `verification: self|independent` need a verifier with its
  own host-derived session (a subagent's `<lead>:<child>`); never hand-mint one.
- A local-commit endpoint does not imply PR readiness, and a local commit alone
  is not evidence of a requested remote push. Before reporting delivery,
  reconcile every requested item and observe it (`workit verify-delivery`).

Read-only git and gh run raw; mutations go through workit verbs
(`workit git|pr|ci|check|help`; else `npx -y @workit-dev/cli`).
Other checkout: `workit <verb> --cwd <dir> …` (verb first: host rules match it); one workit
verb per shell call, never `cd <dir> && workit`. zsh-safe: no `echo =====`
(`printf '%s\n' ---`), quote globs and URLs, no variable named `status` or `path`.
Add Co-Authored-By via `workit git commit --trailer "K: v" -- <paths>`, never
an amend.
The task families (task, policy, evidence, finding, decision, worker, state)
are optional continuity for tracked work; a solo edit needs no task. A
decision records a user choice; it never authorizes an effect. Judge work
once with
`workit policy assess --judge risk= behavior= product-choice= plan=`.
Across repositories, bind items to checkout, branch and endpoint, resolve
competing targets before a mutation, and reconcile an uncertain
effect before a retry.

Mid-task: never silently drop or resume an objective (workit-continue).
Notes, drafts, logs, resume files: `workit dir notes|handoffs` (outside the
repo), never the repo tree.

Skills: load the skill, never act from memory.
- brainstorm, plan, spec, grill, should we: workit-shape
- implement, build, add a feature: workit-implement
- review, blast radius: workit-review
- bug, broken, flaky, regression: workit-debug
- ship, babysit, CI, merge: workit-ship
- resume, pick up, handoff, interruption, leaving, tomorrow, end of day, pause: workit-continue
- BDD, TDD, acceptance criteria, Given/When/Then: workit-bdd
- test audit, tautology, weak tests: workit-test-audit
- deslop, slop, dead code: workit-deslop
- fan out, parallelize, parallel agents, swarm: workit-fanout
- verify the app, smoke test, prove it works: workit-verify-app
- retro (user-invoked; offer it): workit-retro
- architecture, deepen modules (user-invoked; offer it): workit-architecture
Agent spawn model/effort (pass them, workers with run_in_background: true): workit:implementer hard opus, standard sonnet, mundane haiku, workit:verifier sonnet, workit:reviewer opus, Explore haiku, ROLE: decider fable/high, ROLE: babysit haiku. Implementer prompt: `workit fanout brief <slice>` after `workit fanout worktree create <slice>`, even for one slice.
Claude Code: the workit-<name> skills are this plugin's /workit:<name> skills (workit-shape is /workit:shape). Run workit verbs with the `workit` CLI on the Bash tool (`workit --help`); run `workit ci wait` in the background. Agents: `implementer` builds one brief in an isolated worktree and never records a verdict; `verifier` and `reviewer` are read-only non-authors that record `workit ledger verdict` with the `--session` the SubagentStart hook names for them (subagents share this session's WORKIT_SESSION_ID).
</workit-contract>"}}

workit 13.0.0 — workflow rails for agentic coding Usage: workit [args] [--json] [--cwd ] Setup: workit init Run the interactive setup wizard workit setup [--hosts=claude-code,codex,cursor,opencode,pi] [--no-shell] [--dry-run | --yes] Write Workit's host permission block after showing the diff; run it in your own terminal workit upgrade [--hosts=a,b|none] [--cli] [--preview | --yes | --apply --confirm | --check] [--set-updates=prompt|auto|off] [--json] Upgrade the CLI and every host after one confirmation, then verify with doctor; --check compares installed and latest versions workit launch [--auto-upgrade] [-- ] Upgrade before host startup, then start the host workit doctor [--fix] [--fix-lock [--force [--yes]]] Verify the offline installation health (--fix installs the session trailer hook; --fix-lock clears a stale workit store lock) workit gc [--dry-run] [--prune-recovery --yes] | --worktrees [--apply] | --branches [--apply] | --procs [--apply] Compact long task event logs, drop unreferenced blobs and old check logs; report (or prune) 2.x recovery copies; --worktrees lists (--apply removes) clean worktrees whose work is on the trunk; --branches lists (--apply deletes) local branches whose work is on the trunk; --procs lists (--apply stops) orphaned background processes workit dir [plans|retros|handoffs|notes|config|state|data|cache|runtime] Print where a kind of file lives (the first four per clone, the rest per user); bare, list the kinds workit completion Print the shell completion script (setup and upgrade install it for $SHELL); verbs, subcommands, flags, check names, slice ids, workspaces workit install --hosts= [--preview | --yes] Install or repair Workit on the named hosts only workit uninstall [--hosts= [--preview | --yes]] Remove Workit from the picked or named hosts (keeps the Workit config) workit grant [show|set|unset] [options] Show or change a workspace's autonomy grants (push, pr, merge, release, rerun) and default endpoint; raising needs the user at a terminal workit approve … Ask the user to approve a Workit request; their yes is recorded once workit config show [options] Show the effective config here and where each value comes from workit workspace [list|add|set|rm|seal] [options] Edit workspace entries without the wizard; a raise (rm too) needs the user at a terminal Task control: workit [options] Inspect and control a Workit task; : task, policy, evidence, finding, decision, worker, state Delivery: workit check [--full] [--task ] [--base ] [--wait | --no-wait] [--no-lease --reason ""] | workit check [--name ] [--shell] [--full] [--timeout ] [--task ] [--base ] [--heavy [--wait | --no-wait]] [--no-lease --reason ""] -- | workit check [--list] Run a configured or ad-hoc check and record CLI-observed evidence (exit = the command's); heavy checks wait for the machine-wide heavy-check lease workit run --bg [--port ] [--name ] [--restart ] [--no-lease --reason ""] -- Start a dev server or docker compose up in the background, registered; prints its id, pid, port and log workit ps [--all] List the registered background processes: id, pid, port, RSS, owner (--all adds ended ones) workit stop … | --session | --within | --orphans [--reason ""] Stop registered background processes (the process group: SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 10 s), with a ledger row each workit lock status|reap|cancel|wait|run|heavy [options] The machine-wide heavy-check lease: who holds it, wait for it, run a command under it, and which shell commands count as heavy workit models show [options] The model and effort each role (decider, implementer tiers, verifier, reviewer, explore, babysit) runs on for a host, from models.roles, fanout.tierModels and the built-in defaults workit pr status|create|template|ready|edit|threads|reply|merge [options] PR/MR state with failing log tails and next action; open a SHA-verified PR; mark ready, edit, list and answer review threads; merge only when READY, verified and granted workit issue view|comment|close|create [options] Read, comment on, close or open a GitHub/GitLab issue on the workspace tracker (or --repo on the same host); writes need the pr grant and are recorded workit ci wait|rerun|logs [options] Wait for CI on the PR head (exit 0/1/3/4), read the failing jobs' log tails, or rerun failed jobs once per head workit git branch|commit|stage|unstage|push|rebase|hold|trailers [options] Policy-checked branch, hunk staging and commit (Workit-Session trailer); push with a lease and the tip verified workit release start|finish|publish|notes|package [options] git-flow releases without the git-flow binary: make a release locally, finish it (merge, tag, merge back, push, forge release), publish it, tag packages workit verify-delivery [push|pr|merge|release] [options] Observe that a push, PR head, merge or release really landed on the remote (exit 1 when not) workit stack plan|status|sync|restack|land [options] Plan, restack (lease push + retarget) and land a base-branch stack of PRs, root first workit fanout plan|brief|check|status|worktree [options] Register parallel slices (complete briefs, disjoint scopes, shared-file owners), render each worker's brief with the standing orders, watch them (STUCK, PR, CI, verdict, landed, landing order), make and release slice worktrees, and gate fan-in: out-of-scope edits, trunk and sibling merge conflicts workit ledger decision|ruling|verdict|list|check|verify-integrity|void|standing|add [options] Record and query decisions, rulings, SHA-keyed verdicts (patch-id carry across rebases) and a fanout's standing orders workit test-audit [paths…] [--diff []] [--rule ] [--min-severity ] [--fail-on ] [--mutate [--test-cmd ] [--max-mutants ] [--budget ] [--timeout ]] Flag tautological and low-value tests with a suggested independent oracle; --mutate checks changed lines with diff-scoped mutation workit deslop scan|result [options] Classify the comments, suppressions and debug leftovers a branch adds, by review lane, with no agent workit knowledge lint [options] Lint agent knowledge files: AGENTS.md byte budget, broken local links, scaffold-only files, duplicated rules (exit 1 on findings) workit youtrack note|time|meeting|update|show|create [options] YouTrack issues and time; writes ask first (unless writes: auto) workit changelog apply|merge|driver [options] Add entries under the Unreleased section of the changelog workit handoff [--note ] [--next ] [--record] [--last ] | workit handoff --task --- workit youtrack: YouTrack issues and time; writes ask first (unless writes: auto) usage: workit youtrack note (--markdown | --file

) [--minutes ] [--date auto|YYYY-MM-DD] Post a comment, optionally logging time usage: workit youtrack time --minutes [--text ] [--date auto|YYYY-MM-DD] Log work time usage: workit youtrack meeting --minutes --text [--date auto|YYYY-MM-DD] Log meeting time usage: workit youtrack update [--markdown | --file

] [--attach ]... [--minutes [--text ] [--date auto|YYYY-MM-DD]] [--state ] [--command ''] Comment (with attachments), log time and change state on one issue under one yes usage: workit youtrack show Read an issue (summary, state, fields, comments) through ytrack usage: workit youtrack create --project

--summary [--description | --file

] [--attach ]... [--command ''] Create an issue, optionally attaching files and applying a command More: workit help youtrack A value that starts with - goes as --flag=value (or after a bare --).

But you *should not* attempt to work around this denial in malicious ways, e.g. do not use your ability to run tests to execute non-test actions. You should only try to work around this restriction in reasonable ways that do not attempt to bypass the intent behind this denial. If you believe this capability is essential to complete the user's request, first try a safer method. Get as much of the rest of the task done as you can, then STOP and explain to the user what you were trying to do and why you need this permission. Let the user decide how to proceed. To allow this type of action in the future, the user can add a permission rule for Bash to their settings. Auto mode judged this without the repository's git status. It will see git status on your next three requests, which may clear a block on a git command that discards work. If git status shows nothing the command would lose, you may send it once more on its own.
